To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the analysis of periodic lines can be performed by the electromagnetic simulation of truncated structures, and that the number of cells to be simulated is determined by the convergence of the modal solutions.

(1) the Bloch analysis of periodic structures is based on the simulation of truncated structures, (2) the number of simulated spatial periods must be increased until the convergence of the results is verified, and (3) spurious solutions are related to the non-uniqueness of root extraction in the complex plane, and a simple method is provided to recover the correct results.

(a) the simulation of a finite number of spatial cells of the line is needed to accurately extract the Bloch modes, and that (b) the correct solution of the Bloch modes can be obtained by means of an automatic method that exploits the nonuniquenes of root-extraction algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of one-dimensional periodic structures, and in particular, with the accurate extraction of the dispersion diagram of a periodic waveguide.
the analysis of 1-D periodic lines, which are characterized by the presence of a periodic distribution of inhomogeneities.
the development of a new method for the analysis of one-dimensional periodic structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in order to achieve an accurate analysis of a periodic structure, it is necessary to simulate a sufficiently large portion of the structure.
a single-cell approach is not recommended for the analysis of periodic structures, since the resulting equivalent two-ports are not suitable for accurate dispersive analysis.

, when the number of simulated unit cells is small, the method proposed in this paper should be preferred, since it is more robust, more efficient, and less prone to spurious solutions than other methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a periodic line with period d and number of periods L, the Bloch modes are obtained by simulating L cells, provided that the number of cells is odd and the number of ports is equal to the number of cells.
the Bloch mode analysis of 1D periodic structures is not as simple as it seems.
the Bloch-Floquet analysis is the only rigorous approach to obtain the modal dispersion diagram of periodic lines, but it is also the most time-consuming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a Bloch analysis based on the simulation of a single cell is generally inaccurate.

the simulation of the single period of the structure is sufficient to obtain a correct analysis of the modal properties of 1-D periodic lines, provided that the Bloch-Floquet modes are properly extracted.
, for accurate Bloch analysis, it is mandatory to simulate at least two cells.
